To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FXR regulates expression of C3, a secreted factor that influences lipid metabolism.
FXR regulates expression of complement C3 and Fgf15 and that the C3 gene promoter contains functional FXR response element(s).
FXR is a nuclear receptor that regulates the expression of secreted factors that influence lipid metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms by which the nuclear bile acid receptor FXR regulates gene expression in the liver and intestine.
the regulation of gene expression by the nuclear receptor farnesoid-X-receptor (FXR; also known as NR1H4).
the regulation of the complement component C3 gene, which plays a critical role not only in the immune system but also in lipid and glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bile acid levels are inversely related to triglyceride levels, and that FXR is a key regulator of this process.
FXR regulates complement C3 gene transcription by direct binding to the C3 promoter.
the FXR is a key regulator of bile acid metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bile acid sensing through FXR regulates the synthesis and secretion of C3, which in turn may affect lipid metabolism.
FXR regulates complement C3 expression in hepatocytes and that FXR agonists increase the circulating levels of complement C3 in rats.
FXR regulates expression of complement C3 and Fgf15, which in turn regulate lipid metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

FXR regulates not only the synthesis of bile acids but also the secretion of factors such as FGF15 and complement C3 that have a direct effect on lipid metabolism in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner.
FXR regulates secretion of factors such as complement C3 that have the capacity to influence lipid metabolism.
FXR regulates not only bile acid homeostasis but also lipid and energy metabolism.
